findings: The A20 and A23 spawn/proof/cleanup functions are unchanged; successful A23 rounds do not establish a fix for this shared path.
The acceptance predicate requires a pidfd, a successful terminal probe, and either confirmed termination or matching UID/executable inode/argv.

The generic error does not retain pidfd errno or the identity-read failure stage. A short-lived-process race, a resource failure, and an actual identity mismatch cannot be distinguished from this record.

The exact final refusal text is emitted only after stop_child and release return successfully. The original owned child was therefore reaped and removed from its ledger; this does not establish that its command never executed.
The shared pool stop token is cancelled before that cleanup. One explicit proof refusal was recorded alongside 179 other timed stopped/unavailable refusals and six final-output-check refusals.
All four controllers later exited zero through stdin EOF with no recorded reader errors, unmatched responses, or observed descendant survivors.
A separate same-parameter r02 will remain a distinct experiment, with r01 retained. Passing r02 would not resolve this unclassified shared lifecycle risk.
next_action: Preserve the original proof predicate, stop timing and cleanup. Add opt-in fixed-category failure diagnostics to an isolated diagnostic build; do not weaken identity validation or retry execution.
